issues.t: Severe frame rust
issues.sym: Thick flaking scale, holes, or soft spots on the frame rails, and parts bolted to the frame (sway bar, steering rack, fuel tank straps) coming loose.
issues.why: The frame's rust protection did not hold up on salted winter roads. Toyota offered frame replacement on 2000-2003 trucks and later corrosion-proofing campaigns, but many owners report rot on trucks outside those programs.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected soon, including tapping suspect areas. A badly rotted frame is unsafe to drive or tow with. Ask a Toyota dealer whether any program still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Rear crossmember rust can drop the spare tire (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or clunking from under the rear, a sagging spare tire, or visible rot on the rear crossmember.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the rear crossmember that holds the spare tire carrier. If it weakens enough, the spare can fall off while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the rear crossmember inspected right away. Do not drive with a loose or sagging spare.

issues.t: Front ball joint wear and separation
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering steering, uneven tire wear, or in the worst case a front wheel suddenly collapsing or folding under the truck.
issues.why: The front ball joints on these trucks wear out and owners report them separating, sometimes at low speed while turning. Rust around the suspension mounts makes things worse.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked for play now, especially on a high-mileage truck. If you hear clunks from the front end, get it inspected before driving at speed.

issues.t: Secondary air pump failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, a whining noise at cold start, and sometimes reduced power or limp mode.
issues.why: The air pump that helps heat the catalytic converters after a cold start can fail. Unlike later trucks, these years were not included in Toyota's extended coverage.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pump and valves tested. If the truck goes into limp mode, get it diagnosed before relying on it for towing or highway trips.

issues.t: Secondary air injection pump or valve failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, a loud noise right after a cold start, and sometimes the truck drops into reduced power mode.
issues.why: The air pumps and their switching valves can take in water and debris, which rusts them inside until they seize or stick. Toyota extended coverage on the pumps and valves for 2007-2010 trucks.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pumps and valves tested. Ask a Toyota dealer whether the extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Frame rust (frame replacement program)
issues.sym: Heavy scaling, flaking or holes on the frame, often worst in snowy, salted-road states.
issues.why: Some frames from these years were not protected well enough against road salt. Toyota ran a frame replacement program and a corrosion-proofing campaign for certain trucks.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected promptly. Do not tow with a frame that shows holes or soft spots. Ask a Toyota dealer whether your VIN was part of the frame programs.

issues.t: Leaking water pump
issues.sym: Pink crusty residue or drips at the front of the engine, low coolant, weak heat, or the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: The water pump's bearing and seal wear over time and start to leak coolant.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and replace a leaking pump before it lets the engine overheat.

issues.t: Cam tower oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping at the back of the cylinder heads, a burning oil smell after driving, and a slowly dropping oil level.
issues.why: The sealant between the cam towers and cylinder heads can break down. Oil can then drip onto the hot exhaust manifold. The proper repair is labor heavy because the engine timing has to be taken apart.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the leak confirmed. Because oil can land on the exhaust, get it repaired rather than ignoring it.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold or leaking gasket
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping sound that is loudest on a cold start and may fade as the engine warms up.
issues.why: Repeated heating and cooling can crack the exhaust manifold or wear out its gasket. Heavy towing speeds this up.
issues.next: Have the manifolds inspected. Repair it before the leak grows or starts to affect the oxygen sensors.

issues.t: Rear driveshaft clunk
issues.sym: A clunk or thunk from under the truck when pulling away from a stop or shifting, sometimes with a slight vibration.
issues.why: Wear and binding in the rear driveshaft slip joint on four-wheel-drive trucks. Toyota issued service bulletins for the noise.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check the driveshaft against the bulletin. It is usually a noise issue, but have worn joints replaced.

issues.t: Rear axle bearing howl
issues.sym: A howl or growl from the rear of the truck that gets louder as speed increases.
issues.why: A worn rear axle bearing. Toyota published a bulletin for replacing the bearing to fix the noise.
issues.next: Have the rear axle bearings checked soon. A failing bearing gets worse and can damage the axle if ignored.

issues.t: ABS, brake and 4WD warning lights on together
issues.sym: The ABS, brake and four-wheel-drive lights come on at the same time.
issues.why: A fault in the brake actuator assembly can set communication and speed sensor codes. Toyota's bulletin calls for replacing the actuator.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon. Normal braking usually remains, but ABS and stability help may be off until it is fixed.

issues.t: Valve timing codes from a stiff VVT spring
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing codes, sometimes with slightly rough running.
issues.why: Some engines were built with a variable valve timing spring that is too stiff, so the system can stick in the wrong position.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin for this fix.

issues.t: Front brake vibration
issues.sym: A shaking or pulsing in the steering wheel or brake pedal when slowing down.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for front brake vibration on these trucks, usually tied to the front rotors.
issues.next: Have the front brakes inspected and ask the dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Charcoal canister contamination
issues.sym: Check engine light for the evaporative emissions system.
issues.why: Water or dirt can get in through the fresh air inlet of the fuel vapor canister. Toyota revised the filler pipe to help prevent it.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin for this repair.

issues.t: Twin-turbo V6 main bearing failure (recalls)
issues.sym: Engine knocking, rough running, loss of power, stalling while driving, or the engine not starting.
issues.why: Machining debris left inside some engines at the factory can stick to the crankshaft main bearings and wear them out. Toyota has issued several recalls to inspect the bearing or replace the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls now. Toyota's later recall advises not driving affected trucks until the dealer inspects them. If the engine knocks or runs rough, stop and have it towed.

issues.t: Rear axle shaft nuts can loosen (recall 22V-445)
issues.sym: Clunk, vibration or gear oil at a rear wheel. In the worst case an axle shaft and wheel can come away.
issues.why: Nuts on the rear axle flange may not have been tightened enough and can back off.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear new rear axle noise and have the recall done. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Fuel tube can rub on a brake line and leak (recall 23V-566)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or wet fuel under the truck.
issues.why: A plastic fuel tube can chafe against a brake line until it wears through.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell fuel, because of the fire risk. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Truck can creep forward in Neutral (recall 24V-125)
issues.sym: With the shifter in Neutral and your foot off the brake, the truck can move forward on level ground.
issues.why: Parts inside the automatic transmission may not fully release, so some drive still reaches the wheels.
issues.next: Keep the brake applied in Neutral and get the software update promptly. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Instrument panel screen can go blank (recall 23V-111)
issues.sym: The digital gauge display goes dark, so speed and warning lights are not shown.
issues.why: A software error in the instrument cluster.
issues.next: Get the software update soon. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not display (recalls)
issues.sym: Blank, frozen or wrong camera picture when backing up.
issues.why: Several software faults in the parking assist system can keep the rear camera image off the screen.
issues.next: Check behind you by other means and get the update soon. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Reverse lights can fail from moisture (recall 25V-322)
issues.sym: One or both white reverse lights stop working.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the reverse light assemblies and corrode them.
issues.next: Have them replaced when you can. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Electric parking brake may not engage (recall 22V-661)
issues.sym: Parking brake warning message, and the parking brake may not set.
issues.why: The brake control computer can wrongly detect an electrical fault and refuse to apply the parking brake.
issues.next: Make sure the truck is in Park and get the update soon. The repair is free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see if it was already done.

issues.t: Power steering gear can leak
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid dripping under the front of the truck, a low reservoir, a whine when turning, or heavier steering.
issues.why: The hydraulic steering gear assembly can leak oil from its seals.
issues.next: Have the gear inspected and replaced. Check the VIN for recalls 21V-920 and 21E-103, and do not let the reservoir run dry.

issues.t: High and low beams can power together and overheat the wiring
issues.sym: Headlights flicker or go out, or there is a hot plastic smell from a headlight.
issues.why: Both beams can be powered at once, which overloads a connector in the headlight harness.
issues.next: Have the harness modified under recall 21V-688 and any melted parts replaced before you lose a headlight at night.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine
issues.sym: A rough idle, a check engine light, hard starting, or the engine cutting out while driving and not restarting.
issues.why: The in-tank low pressure fuel pump can stop delivering fuel.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 20V-682 and have the pump replaced. A stall in traffic is dangerous, so do not put this off.

issues.t: Front turn signals may not flash brightly enough
issues.sym: The front blinkers look dim and are hard for other drivers to see in daylight.
issues.why: The wiring to the front turn signals does not give them enough power.
issues.next: Have the harness modified under recall 20V-410, and use hand signals or extra care at busy junctions until then.

issues.t: Accessory dual exhaust can rub a brake line
issues.sym: A low brake pedal, a brake warning light, or fluid dripping near a rear wheel on a truck with the add-on dual exhaust.
issues.why: The accessory exhaust was routed close enough to a brake line to wear through it.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Stop driving if the pedal sinks. Check the VIN for recall 05V-123 and have the exhaust and the brake line inspected.

issues.t: Load capacity label may show the wrong weight
issues.sym: Nothing is wrong with the truck, but the door jamb sticker overstates how much weight you can add.
issues.why: The label did not account for accessories fitted before delivery, so the stated carrying capacity is too high.
issues.next: Get the corrected label free from a dealer and go by the new figure when loading the bed or hitching a trailer.
